activity.notes: Herodotus presents Arganthonios as king of Tartessos and links him personally to the Phocaeans. Modern Spanish scholarship strongly questions the individual's historicity and identifies the reported eighty-year reign and 120-year lifespan as mythic or literary constructions. Other archaeological-historical work nevertheless treats Phocaean contact with Arganthonios in the sixth-century BCE Tartessian context and places the aid to threatened Phocaea around the mid-sixth century. ATLAS therefore does not use the conventional 80-year reign rail; it records only c.550 BCE as a disputed approximate point tied to the historically situated Phocaean episode.

sources.citation_text: Padilla Monge identifies strong mythic and literary features in Arganthonios' longevity, chronology, name, and Phocaean narrative and substantially questions the historicity of the individual.

sources.citation_text: The CSIC-led study treats Arganthonios within the historical sixth-century BCE Tartessian and Phocaean contact context and notes that he was dead by the time of the later Phocaean displacement.
